accuracy.evidence: Boiling points C1–C20 in the lab (−162, −89, −42, −1, 36, 69, 98, 126 … 343 °C) match NIST WebBook/CRC values to the nearest degree; states at 20 °C follow (C1–C4 gas, C5–C16 liquid since hexadecane melts at 18 °C, C17+ solid since heptadecane melts at 22 °C). Flash points hexane −22, decane 46, hexadecane 135 °C from PubChem; viscosity ratios from 20–25 °C data. Explanation matches AQA 4.7.1.2 wording.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented GCSE errors: covalent bonds breaking on boiling (boil step shows molecules leaving whole; p1, m1, challenge 'bonds'), heaviness instead of forces as the cause of viscosity (m6), reversed flammability trend (m4, m8), stating trends without the cause chain (link step, p5), and the C1–C4 gas boundary (m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagalktr is about how chain length affects bulk properties: a plotted homologous-series boiling point curve, a thermometer that separates two chains held by contact forces, a 20-tube room-temperature panel, a viscosity race and a flammability test. flagalk (121) builds formulas, flagimf compares force types; lab gate shingle overlap under 30% with all flag_*.js.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner builds the trend from data (plots C1–C8), sees why (decane needs 174 °C versus 36 °C because more contacts), applies it (finds pentane as first liquid at 20 °C), observes viscosity and flammability consequences, and then assembles the cause-to-effect explanation themselves.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'falls' for boiling point, 'C–C and C–H bonds' for what boiling overcomes, 'C1 to C10' gases at 20 °C, 'hexadecane' flows faster, and 'all the same' for flammability.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions with feedback tied to the slip: bonds vs intermolecular forces, 'fewer hydrogens' (octane has more), liquid/solid for butane at 20 °C, viscosity direction, flammability direction, a falling trend, and an out-of-range interpolation for hexane.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text uses short sentences and defines viscosity, volatile and intermolecular forces in plain words; validator FK check passes the learner targets (kid 6.5, adult 9.5). Precise GCSE terms used: homologous series, intermolecular forces, viscosity, flammability, volatility.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate found no filler phrases; every kid paragraph carries one link in the explanation (series, trend with values, cause, consequences) and adult text gives spec reference, mechanism, named mistakes and lab summary.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light for all 7 steps: chain, graph axes, 20 tubes (2 rows of 10), funnels, dishes and five link cards are readable without clipping; buttons wrap below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: All drags have button twins (+/− carbon, Pentane/Decane/Heat +20 °C, C3–C6 choice, Pour, Light C6/C10/C16, each link card as a button); the canvas aria-label narrates each result; walk.cjs axe clean in both themes on desktop and phone.

sources: AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) specification 4.7.1.2 Properties of hydrocarbons
NIST Chemistry WebBook / CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics: normal boiling and melting points of n-alkanes C1–C20
PubChem compound records for hexane, decane and hexadecane (flash points, viscosity)
